issues.observed: MonthName is plotted in a non-chronological sequence such as April, August, December, February and January. The line therefore connects unrelated points and presents a false time progression.
issues.desired: Months must follow the fiscal or calendar chronology appropriate to the selected period.
issues.action: Create or use a numeric MonthSort or FiscalMonthNumber column, set MonthName to Sort by column, and verify chronological order for every fiscal-year context.

issues.observed: The gross-margin trend also uses non-chronological month ordering, making the apparent rises and falls analytically misleading.
issues.desired: A chronologically ordered monthly margin trend with an unambiguous fiscal-year sequence.
issues.action: Apply the same fiscal month sort key used by the revenue trend and test the ordering when one or multiple fiscal years are selected.

issues.observed: The slicers visibly feature FY 2022, London and Beauty while the charts still show two fiscal years, London plus Scotland, and several categories. The current selection state is unclear and may indicate disabled or disconnected visual interactions.
issues.desired: Executives should be able to see the active filter state immediately, and all applicable visuals should respond consistently.
issues.action: Validate slicer relationships and Edit interactions for every visual. Use compact dropdown slicers with explicit 'All' or selected-value text, and add a visible reset-filters control. If the displayed values are not selected, redesign the slicers so that state cannot be mistaken for a selection.

issues.observed: TotalRevenue and YoYGrowthPct are plotted against a shared currency-scale presentation. Revenue columns dominate while the percentage series is effectively reduced to tiny marks at the baseline.
issues.desired: Revenue magnitude and growth rate should both be readable without implying that currency and percentage share a common scale.
issues.action: Use a native line-and-clustered-column chart with revenue on the primary axis and YoY growth on the percentage secondary axis. Add growth labels, a zero reference line, and semantic positive/negative colouring.

issues.observed: The horizontal category bars make revenue readable, but YoYGrowthPct is represented by negligible red marks on the revenue scale and cannot be compared meaningfully.
issues.desired: A ranked category view that clearly communicates both revenue contribution and positive or negative growth.
issues.action: Keep revenue bars sorted descending and expose YoY growth through percentage data labels, conditional icons, or a separate aligned growth panel. Do not plot percentages directly on the currency axis.

issues.observed: A prominent Power BI trial-capacity banner is visible across the top of the deployed page.
issues.desired: A production executive dashboard without licensing, trial or development notices.
issues.action: Deploy the report through appropriately licensed production capacity or remove the trial-capacity condition before presenting it to CEO/CFO audiences.

issues.observed: Large saturated green bands and an empty white strip consume substantial space above and behind the slicers without providing a page title, context or analytical content.
issues.desired: A restrained header containing the page title, reporting-period context, compact filters and optional last-refresh information.
issues.action: Remove the oversized decorative shapes. Introduce a compact 48-64 pixel header and move the slicers into a single aligned row so more height is available for analytical visuals.

issues.observed: Cards and chart titles expose model-style names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarginPct, YoYGrowthPct and RiskCount. Several titles use auto-generated 'by MonthName and FiscalYear' wording.
issues.desired: Plain-language executive labels such as Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth, Risk Areas, Revenue Trend and Gross Margin % Trend.
issues.action: Rename fields for each visual or use explicit titles. Apply consistent title case and remove redundant technical field lists from chart titles.

issues.observed: The four headline values are visible but provide no comparison period, variance indicator, target status or explanation of what constitutes a risk area.
issues.desired: Each KPI should communicate value, period context and decision significance at a glance.
issues.action: Add concise comparison subtitles such as 'vs prior year' and conditional variance indicators based on existing approved measures. Add a tooltip defining Risk Areas and its threshold logic; do not invent target semantics if no governed measure exists.

issues.observed: The KPI formatting is generic: values use subdued blue-gray text, RiskCount has no risk-state emphasis, and card borders rely on the surrounding green blocks rather than a refined component system.
issues.desired: Prominent, consistently formatted KPI values with controlled semantic colour and subtle card separation.
issues.action: Increase KPI value weight and contrast, use neutral card backgrounds with subtle borders or shadows, and apply warning colour to RiskCount only when supported by governed threshold logic.

issues.observed: The lower visuals are compressed into limited height, producing diagonal month labels, small legends and a partially crowded gross-margin chart while decorative header space remains unused.
issues.desired: Readable charts with horizontal or minimally rotated labels and enough plot area for pattern recognition.
issues.action: Reclaim header space, use a two-row chart grid, and increase the height of the trend visuals. Reduce label density only after chronological sorting, and use concise month abbreviations.

issues.observed: The page presents values and charts but does not direct attention to the principal revenue driver, margin movement, declining region or declining category. Negative growth is almost invisible in the comparison charts.
issues.desired: A clear executive narrative linking headline performance to the regions and categories responsible for improvement or risk.
issues.action: Use descending ranking, visible zero lines, positive/negative growth labels and concise dynamic subtitles based only on governed measures. Emphasize exceptions rather than applying strong colour to large decorative areas.

issues.observed: Axis labels, legends and category labels are very small relative to the page and are unlikely to remain readable in a boardroom or shared-screen setting.
issues.desired: A restrained but presentation-safe type scale with clear contrast between page title, KPI values, visual titles and supporting labels.
issues.action: Define a report-wide type hierarchy and increase chart labels and legends to approximately 10-12 pt at the target canvas size. Use larger visual titles and avoid low-contrast gray for essential text.

issues.observed: Highly saturated green is used for large structural areas, revenue series and fiscal-year encoding, while red serves both a second year and growth measures. This weakens semantic consistency and overwhelms the data.
issues.desired: A neutral canvas with one primary brand colour and reserved semantic colours for favorable and unfavorable outcomes.
issues.action: Use neutral page and card backgrounds, a consistent primary series colour for revenue, and reserve green/red for performance direction only. Distinguish fiscal years with related non-semantic hues or line styles.

issues.observed: The four KPI cards align reasonably well, but slicer widths, chart gutters, borders and visual heights do not form a fully consistent grid.
issues.desired: Consistent outer margins, gutters, card padding and row heights across the page.
issues.action: Apply a fixed grid with equal KPI widths, consistent 12-16 pixel gutters, aligned chart edges and uniform internal padding.

summary: The deployed page contains all major required KPI and performance views, so its analytical foundation is present. However, non-chronological month sorting makes both trends misleading, mixed currency/percentage scales make growth unreadable, and the visible filter state may not match chart results. Oversized green decoration, technical labels, small typography and the trial banner substantially reduce executive credibility. Most deficiencies are achievable Power BI design, modeling and layout fixes rather than platform constraints.
reference_rejected_ideas: Exact recreation of the Power BI service navigation rail, toolbar and utility icons is outside the analytical report canvas and is not necessary for executive decision-making.

The reference's horizontal revenue bars with independently scaled YoY dot markers are not a standard native Power BI combo configuration. Use aligned visuals, labels or a certified custom visual rather than forcing unlike measures onto one axis.
KPI sparklines and information icons are optional enhancements, not analytical requirements; add them only when governed historical data and useful tooltip definitions are available.
Pixel-level imitation of the reference's shadows, chrome and decorative styling should not take priority over chronological sorting, correct filter interactions and readable measure scales.
